lines.text: So — I had my three questions. Rider support cost, down twenty percent, by end of Q3.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: I had the frame. [pause] Now I needed the data.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Day two. [pause] I walk in ready to work.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Finance drops this on my desk.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: One CSV. [pause] Forty-thousand rows.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Column headers like t-k-t-closed-d-t-v-two. I had no idea what that meant.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: It's a menu in a language I don't speak.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: I stare at the names. Trying to decode them.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Ticket closed dt v2? Rider seg enc? Supp contact flag three?
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Half the words are abbreviated. I'm inventing meanings as I go.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Marco walks past. Sees me squinting. He goes — what does that one actually mean? I had no idea.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Headers lie.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: That one column — could mean the first time a ticket was closed.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Or the final close, after re-opens.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Count the first-closes, tickets look flat. Count the finals, tickets look doubled.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Same column. [pause] Two totally different realities.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Before you analyze — you translate.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: For every column I'd use, three questions.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: What does it actually mean — in plain English.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Where does it come from — who writes to it.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: And — what does it not tell me.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Whole afternoon. [pause] Just a notebook and the CSV open.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: One line per column. In my own words.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Half of them I ended up DMing Jorge — the finance guy who shipped the export.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: By sundown I could read the dataset like a newspaper.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Airbnb's dataset is going to be messier than mine was.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Host-support tickets. Refunds. Disputes. Cancellations. Policy flags.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Before you run a single query — build the glossary.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Translate first. [pause] Then analyze.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Alright — your turn.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: I'll show you three columns from an Airbnb slice. Pick what each one actually means.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: I did this with a notebook in 2023. Today? I'd just drop the CSV in here and ask.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Thirty seconds. Same shape I spent an afternoon on. But watch — Claude just took the obvious read. Exactly the trap that almost got me.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: So I push back with what I know. Claude corrects. I only caught it because I'd already done the work.
lines.speaker: avery

lines.text: Use the tool. Don't outsource the thinking.
lines.speaker: avery
